gloss: such; that kind of; like that

definitions.gloss: such; that kind of; of that sort
definitions.explanation: Modifies a following noun to point back at something just mentioned or known to the listener. The formal written counterpart of そんな, standard in business letters, official notices, and careful speech.

examples.japanese: そのような{場合|ばあい}はご{連絡|れんらく}ください。
examples.english: Please contact us in such a case.

examples.japanese: そのような{話|はなし}は{聞|き}いたことがありません。
examples.english: I have never heard such a thing.

examples.japanese: そのような{事故|じこ}が{二度|にど}と{起|お}こらないよう、{安全|あんぜん}{対策|たいさく}を{見直|みなお}します。
examples.english: We will review our safety measures so that such an accident never happens again.

notes:
USAGE:
Always followed by a noun. Before a verb or adjective the adverbial form そのように is used instead: そのように{考|かんが}えています (I think along those lines).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- そのような{場合|ばあい}: in such a case
- そのようなこと: such a thing
- そのような{方|かた}: a person of that sort (polite)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- そんな: such, that kind of — the everyday spoken equivalent; そのような is one register higher
- このような: this kind of — for things near the speaker or just introduced by the speaker
- あのような: that kind of — for things distant from both speaker and listener
